name: Sinyar
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2015. Case alignment(s) in Sinyar. In A. Mietzner & A. Storch (eds), Nilo-Saharan: Models and Descriptions, 21-36. Köln: Köppe. (HAL author manuscript halshs-01487206, 17 pp.)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Sec. 2 'Preliminary remarks': 'Sinyar contrasts two level tones (Low/High) and has frequent downstepped Lows (the tonal transcriptions should not be considered as definitive)'; floating tones condition clitic tone. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2020. Central Sudanic languages. In R. Vossen & G. J. Dimmendaal (eds), The Oxford Handbook of African Languages, 408-418. Oxford: OUP. (HAL author manuscript halshs-03097024)
sources.note: Family overview only: 'tone systems that may include up to four contrastive levels'; Sinyar mentioned only for classification (based on Doornbos & Bender 1983). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2019. Is Sinyar an SBB language? Handout, 14th Nilo-Saharan Linguistics Colloquium, Vienna, 29-31 May 2019, 14 pp. (halshs-04579988)
sources.note: Sec. 4 'Tone patterns as evidence for a substrate?' compares Sinyar (2 tones) vs SBB noun/verb tone classes; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2019. Proper names and case markers in Sinyar (Chad/Sudan). STUF - Language Typology and Universals 72(4): 467-504. (HAL author manuscript halshs-03096955, 29 pp.)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Sec. 2.2 'Typological features' item iv: two contrastive level tones (L/H) plus lexical downsteps that may sit word-initially, -internally or -finally; sec. 2.3 notes long vowels and geminates. No mention of stress or accent anywhere (only hit for 'stress' is the verb 'stressed' in an epigraph).

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2013. Sinyar and SBB (Central Sudanic): genetic relationship or contact? Handout, Labex EFL, Paris, July 2013, 12 pp. (halshs-04579986)
sources.note: p.10: 'Sinyar has a two-tone system with numerous downstepped Lows; western SBB languages have no less than three distinctive levels'; 'no tonal alternation on verbs'. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Schadeberg, Thilo C. & M. Lionel Bender (eds). 1981. Nilo-Saharan: Proceedings of the First Nilo-Saharan Linguistics Colloquium, Leiden 1980. Dordrecht: Foris. (archive.org item nilo-saharan-linguistics-colloquim, scanned text)
sources.note: Only isolated Sinyar lexical citations in Bender's isogloss paper (e.g. 'moon' kwan-ja(n)); no Sinyar description; not saved.
'There are two level tones and downstepped low tones' (from Boyeldieu); no stress information; refs = Boyeldieu 2013/2015, Blench CS overview, Blažek 2015.

sources.citation: Doornbos, Paul & M. Lionel Bender. 1983. Languages of Wadai-Darfur. In M. Lionel Bender (ed.), Nilo-Saharan Language Studies (Committee on Northeast African Studies, Monograph 13), 42-79; Sinyar section pp. 70-75. East Lansing: African Studies Center, Michigan State University.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only published pre-Boyeldieu sketch of Sinyar (phonology notes + wordlist from Doornbos's c.1980 fieldwork); Bender's sketches in this chapter usually comment on tone/stress marking, so it is the likeliest place for an explicit stress remark.

sources.citation: Doornbos, Paul. [1980?]. The Language of the Senyar. Unpublished typescript, 15 pp. (copy held by P. Boyeldieu, LLACAN).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: First grammatical sketch of Sinyar; Boyeldieu cites its p.1 remark on 'differences of phonology'; may contain a prosody note. Obtainable only from Boyeldieu or Doornbos's papers (ASC Leiden).

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. Unpublished Sinyar field materials (Khartoum 2009-): grammatical questionnaires, texts, and a provisional Toolbox lexicon of c. 2,000 words; any grammar/lexicon in preparation (cf. HAL talks 2022 'Compound Verbs in Sinyar', 2025 'Yulu, Sinyar, Gula, Fer, and Modo').
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Boyeldieu is the only linguist with substantial modern data; a direct query to him (pascal.boyeldieu@cnrs.fr) is the realistic route to a first-hand statement on whether Sinyar has any stress/accent beside tone.
